items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview
items.q: The first man started me into brass band work was Ernest Rapania, the old drummer.

ctx.x: Did you ever play any parades or have a brass band with that group too?

I don't know. I played in different brass bands, but not with the Young Tuxedo. That's John Kazmi. I worked with every brass band around here, such as… The first man started me into brass band work was Ernest Rapania, the old drummer. Oh, yes. And that was… I was doing them same music in the 20s. And… But you played with him…
Did you play bass or snare drum? I played the snare drum.

items.title: Josiah "Cie" Frazier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: He played the bass drum, and I played the snare drum. That was part of the original tuxedo brass band.

ctx.x: Did they play the same kind of stuff as they played?

It's mostly the same stuff you play in the day. Lots of funeral marches. I'll tell you how the bands did them days. Any band had a funeral march. They'd take the name of it, so the other band wouldn't know the name of it. Yeah, yeah. And the first man that started me on the parade was Ones Trapania, playing the parade. He played the bass drum, and I played the snare drum. That was part of the original tuxedo brass band.

items.title: Josiah 'Cie' Frazier Interview, 1961-02-16
items.q: Ernest Trapanius used that drum in the old WPA band.

ctx.x: that Ernest Trapanius would play and all his dance band drum.
Yeah, Ernest use that drum, Ernest Trapanius used that drum in the old WPA band.
